note:
The household of Sir Ernest Jardine at 9 Clumber Crescent South (#383) on the 1921 return, transcribed by A. Hagues. All ten are bound by number and none is created: every one of them was already in the record as a person, and not one of them carried a 1921 census row, so this adds the year and nothing else.

**The house is certain, and a servant proves it.** Mary Evanson (#1319) is cook at 9 Clumber Crescent South on the 1911 return and cook in this household in 1921 - the same woman in the same kitchen ten years on. The family itself is at the house continuously: the Jardines are returned there in 1901 and 1911, Wright's Directory prints 'Jardine Ernest' on the crescent in 1910-11, 1913-14 and 1915-16, and the 1939 register still finds Ernest and John there. Nothing in this file rests on the order of the enumerator's walk.

**Two O'Connells, a generation apart.** John Granfield O'Connell, 34, born at Napier in New Zealand, is returned as a visitor and gives his trade as managing director of Trent Concrete Ltd, concrete products manufacturers. With him is John Jardine O'Connell, aged 1, born in Nottingham - a child carrying the Jardine name as his middle name, staying in the Jardine house. That is the shape of a marriage between the families, but no schedule here says so and no relationship is written between them beyond what the return gives.

Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way; where the record already holds a birth year it is left alone, since an import fills blanks and never overwrites.
source: 1921 census, 9 Clumber Crescent South, transcribed by A. Hagues. Supporting: the 1901 and 1911 returns for the same house; Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1910-11, 1913-14 and 1915-16, Clumber Crescent South; the 1939 register.
